description: For learners working toward a concept or principle, tasks that require them to explain, compare, predict or justify beyond what was presented, with enough guidance to produce something correct, are expected to improve immediate understanding and near transfer more than tasks completed by recall or copying, with weak evidence for classroom and delayed outcomes and no claim testing cognitive activation as a dimension of teaching quality.
title: Cognitive Activation

description: For a learner who holds a confident but inaccurate explanation, meeting evidence it cannot account for and then being helped to resolve the mismatch is expected to improve conceptual understanding more than the correct account alone, with weak evidence that the revision lasts or that conflict without support helps.
title: Cognitive Disequilibrium

description: Revisiting the same concepts across several cases, perspectives or representations that differ in how the concept applies, with explicit prompts to compare them, is expected to help learners with some but rigid knowledge of an ill-structured domain transfer it to a new case at a short horizon; it may cost factual recall, novices may need a simpler start, and delayed effects are untested here.
title: Cognitive Flexibility

description: Across a sequence, matching how presentation, task order and support distribute processing demand to a learner's current task-specific capacity is expected to improve learning, while keeping effortful processing that the intended outcome and horizon need; in the wiki, single levers and two whole load-reducing designs are tested, the withdraw-and-restore policy is not.
title: Cognitive Load Management

description: For a task-specific novice on high-element-interactivity material, reducing avoidable processing is expected to improve performance or efficiency, a relationship that weakens or reverses as task-specific expertise grows.
title: Cognitive Load Theory

description: For a learner whose attempts stall in a way that looks like a habit of approach (holistic or analytic, quick or deliberate), teaching the approach the task requires to everyone who needs it, faded across sessions, is expected to help more than matching tasks or formats to a measured style; no claim in the wiki tests either use of cognitive styles, and the matching evidence, from learning styles, runs against it.
title: Cognitive Styles

description: When learners study an explanation of something they do not yet understand, leaving out interesting but irrelevant words, pictures, sounds and music (seductive details) is expected to improve comprehension and transfer over the same explanation with them added; the wiki's claims test this, in a meta-analysis and many experiments, and record effects that range from large in one research programme to small or absent elsewhere, depending on the material, its pacing and complexity, and the learner's prior knowledge, working memory and attentional control.
title: Coherence Principle

description: For learners who can take part in the task, working jointly so that each member must engage with the others' reasoning is expected to raise individually measured understanding over working alone on the same task, for goals that gain from explaining and reconciling ideas; co-presence, equal participation or group satisfaction alone are not expected to show it.
title: Collaborative Learning

description: For an adult, often older, learner whose hearing or eyesight has declined, presenting each new item both spoken and written or shown, in a well-lit room with little outside noise and with control of pace, is expected to let them take in more of the new material than speech alone; no claim in the wiki tests this with such learners, only spoken-plus-written words, captions and pacing with other learners.
title: Compensate for age-related sensory impairments by combining audio input with visual presentation

description: For second-language learners building general vocabulary, deliberate study of selected words combined with reading and listening for meaning (glossed, with recurring words) is expected to give more words and better retention than either mode alone, with the deliberate share largest while text coverage is below about 95%; two thin claims test the combination, none tests its order, ratio or dose.
title: Combine intentional and incidental vocabulary learning rather than relying on incidental learning alone

description: For adults and professionals entering a shared practice, sustained and structured participation with more experienced members, under norms of trust and critical inquiry, is proposed to change their practice and understanding over a term or more, though the wiki holds only descriptive, qualitative and argued evidence for it.
title: Communities of Practice

description: For a learner whose coursework stays school-internal, giving the work a real role in a community is associated with civic attitudes, self-reported growth and deeper reflection when the work is tied to course concepts, reflection is structured and relationships are supported; no claim here tests its effect on content learning.
title: Community-Based Learning

description: For learners in a discussion-based course whose shared inquiry stalls at sharing ideas, the CoI framework proposes that designed social, cognitive and teaching presence together move discourse towards resolution, but the wiki holds only survey associations and descriptive profiles of the presences, no test of that effect on learning.
title: Community of Inquiry

description: Scoring a learner's response on a task that represents the intended capability against explicit criteria and a stated threshold, by consistent assessors, is expected to support better teaching, progression and certification decisions than a rank or seat time, though no claim here tests that comparison and assessor agreement is not guaranteed.
title: Competency-Based Assessment

description: When learners must come to understand an abstract symbol system or formal structure (an equation, a group property, a permutation formula), starting with a concrete model of it, moving through an iconic picture of the same model, and ending with the abstract notation, each step explicitly linked to the last, is expected to produce better learning and transfer than starting abstract or staying concrete; one experiment, reported second-hand, tests the full sequence here, a meta-analysis supports concrete materials over symbols alone, and the rest is a review's argument and one teaching experiment.
title: Concreteness Fading

description: For a learner who has committed to a judgment where the evidence could point either way, a prompt to generate specific reasons the opposite could be right, then to decide again, is expected to reduce confirmation, anchoring and overconfidence biases more than a general warning to be objective; no claim in this wiki tests it directly, and the one claim on it rests on a review that names the method without testing it.
title: Considering The Opposite

description: When words and a picture explain one thing and neither makes sense without the other, placing each word next to the part of the picture it describes, and presenting narration at the same time as the animation it describes, is expected to improve learning over separated or successive presentation for learners new to the material; meta-analyses test this (spatial and temporal effects of similar size), with larger effects for complex material and system-paced media and a reversal reported for experienced learners.
title: Contiguity Principle (Spatial and Temporal)

description: For learners who can take part in the task, structured small-group work in which each member's learning is individually checked and counts toward the group's success is expected to raise individually measured achievement over several weeks, more than individualistic or competitive work; grouping alone is not expected to.
title: Cooperative Learning
